key_insight: Euler shifts AI-for-mathematics from just producing answers to organizing the full research process—claims, assumptions, dependencies, failures, and verification—into a shared graph that supports human oversight and multi-agent collaboration.
engineering_relevance: For theorem proving workflows, Euler offers a persistent, structured memory layer that can reduce context loss, improve traceability, and make long-horizon mathematical investigation easier to debug and steer.
method: Builds connected research graphs of statements, assumptions, proof dependencies, alternative approaches, failed attempts, and verification evidence.
Lets agents reuse persistent, task-relevant context across sessions for planning, collaboration, and verification.
Supports human-in-the-loop exploration by allowing users to revisit saved team states and continue reasoning from specific graph nodes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three mathematical research case studies and a software validation of the implemented system.
watch_item: The abstract does not report quantitative benchmark results, so the practical impact and robustness of the graph-based workflow may depend on how well the system scales and how faithfully agents maintain the shared structure.
paper_title: Euler: Towards Human-Centered Multi-Agent Mathematical Discovery
